transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2028-07-25
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ethan Park (Redwood SE), Rajiv Menon (Polaris Head of ML), Kim Alvarez (Platform), Lara Boyd (CTO)
---
Summary: initial integration/discovery for Polaris Cloud evaluating Redwood hosted vs dedicated vs private. Main topics: SDK support (Python/Node), LangChain / LlamaIndex connectors, gateway/proxy patterns, rate-limits and per-route quotas, observability hooks (tracing, token-level cost breakdown), security (KMS, SOC2, VPC).

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood. Ethan's our solutions engineer. We'll run through your integration questions and capture next steps.
[00:18] Lara Boyd: Thanks, Maya. Short context — Polaris runs a managed data platform and we're exploring adding LLM features across several products. We want to understand integration work for hosted vs Dedicated vs private installs.
[00:30] Rajiv Menon: Yes, our core asks: how easy are SDKs, do you have first-class LangChain / LlamaIndex support, and operational controls — rate limits, quotas, and observability. Also security and data residency.
[00:44] Ethan Park: Great, that's exactly what we planned to cover. Quick overview: Redwood provides a hosted API for quick launch, Dedicated for reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput, and Private for VPC/on-prem. SDKs are official for Python and Node, and we maintain community connectors for LangChain and LlamaIndex; Ethan: I can show a snippet later.
[01:10] Kim Alvarez: Quick Q up front — our platform proxies all outbound API calls through an internal gateway for logging and egress controls. Will Redwood work behind a proxy?
[01:20] Ethan Park: Yes, we see that often. For hosted, you can route through your gateway/proxy; we recommend allowing long-lived connections for streaming. For Dedicated and Private, you can also deploy a sidecar gateway or use our VPC peering options to avoid public egress. There can be nuances with TLS termination and client IPs for rate limiting.
[02:05] Rajiv Menon: For rate limits, we need per-customer and per-route quotas. Can we do token-level quotas and per-model caps?
[02:15] Maya Chen: Absolutely. Redwood supports per-route and per-key quotas. You can set per-organization and per-api-key limits, and apply different limits by model. Token-level accounting is available in the usage logs so billing and alerting can use tokens. For Dedicated, you can also enforce hard capacity reservations.
[02:40] Lara Boyd: How does enforcement look? Are limits enforced at the gateway or at the serving runtime? We need to ensure critical traffic isn't throttled unintentionally.
[02:50] Ethan Park: Enforcement happens at the platform edge — request routing layer — so you get consistent throttling behavior before hitting the runtime. For Dedicated, you can reserve capacity so critical routes hit reserved pools. There's also soft limits + burst allowances.
[03:20] Kim Alvarez: Observability — what hooks do we get? We need traces, token-level cost, per-prompt latencies, and per-route dashboards.
[03:30] Ethan Park: Redwood Console exposes per-route and per-model dashboards, token breakdowns, and traces. We emit events and logs to your preferred sinks — Splunk, Datadog, CloudWatch — and you can attach tracing via OpenTelemetry. For Private, logs remain in your VPC. We also provide webhook alert hooks for anomaly detection.
[04:05] Rajiv Menon: Any built-in evals or regression alerts? We run prompt quality monitoring.
[04:12] Maya Chen: We have Redwood Optimize that ties prompt sets to quality metrics and can trigger regression alerts on model changes. For early pilots, we usually export evals and integrate with your existing monitoring.
[04:40] Lara Boyd: Let's talk dev experience. How long to get up and running with the Python SDK and a LangChain pipeline?
[04:50] Ethan Park: For basic generation via SDK it's minutes. LangChain connector is plug-and-play for most LLM APIs — you swap in our client and update a few config values. LlamaIndex has a connector as well; for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) workflows there's a short integration guide. We'll share a small repo.
[05:15] Rajiv Menon: Does Redwood support streaming responses and function/tool calling? We have real-time chat features.
[05:22] Ethan Park: Yes, streaming is supported in SDKs for Python/Node and via server-sent events. Tool/function calling is supported; we also do structured output parsing helpers.
[05:40] Kim Alvarez: On the security front: SOC2, encryption at rest/in transit, KMS/HSM, SSO/SAML for users — what's available for hosted?
[05:50] Maya Chen: Hosted customers get encryption at rest and in transit, and we offer KMS integrations for BYOK in dedicated/private plans. We are SOC 2 Type II; I'll send the SOC2 report. We support SSO/SAML and RBAC in the Console. For the strictest compliance, customers typically go Dedicated or Private and bring their own KMS.
[06:20] Lara Boyd: Data residency — we need EU-only storage for EU customers.
[06:25] Ethan Park: We can pin data to regions in Hosted or use Private deployment in your region. For Dedicated you can choose region-specific clusters. We'll capture the exact EU regions you need.
[06:40] Rajiv Menon: Performance question: we have a latency requirement of sub-200ms 99th for short prompts and bursts to 200 QPS per model during peak. Can Dedicated meet that?
[06:50] Ethan Park: Dedicated is designed for predictable latency and throughput with reserved GPU pools; hitting 200 QPS depends on model size and batching configuration. We can run a benchmark with your prompt templates to baseline — recommended. For sub-200ms 99th, usually smaller models or optimized kernels/quantization help; we can test different quantization profiles.
[07:30] Lara Boyd: About the gateway and IP allowlists — will Redwood require us to open ranges for hosted?
[07:38] Maya Chen: For hosted, yes we provide published egress IP ranges; you can also use a customer-side proxy. For Private or Dedicated in your VPC, you won't need to open public ranges.
[07:55] Kim Alvarez: Any guidance on cost controls? We want to avoid runaway token costs.
[08:05] Ethan Park: We give token-level cost reporting and cost alerts. You can set per-key budgets and per-route caps; Optimize suggests batching and caching settings for cost reduction. Also rate limits can act as hard cost controls.
[08:30] Rajiv Menon: Integration specifics — we prefer LangChain for orchestration. Show us the code-level example?
[08:35] Ethan Park: Sure — (screen share reference) typical LangChain usage is to wrap our Python client as an LLM wrapper. Example: from redwood import RedwoodClient; client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..); then LangChain LLM class takes a call method to generate tokens. Small changes to the prompt and streaming callback are often the only work. We'll put a sample notebook in the repo.
[09:10] Kim Alvarez: For LlamaIndex we use the embedding and index pipelines; what's the embedding model story?
[09:16] Ethan Park: We host several embedding models and provide endpoint parity with generative models. There's token and embedding usage tracking. You can pin embedding model versions and run A/B tests.
[09:35] Lara Boyd: For RAG, does Redwood offer prefix/KV cache or persistent cache hooks?
[09:42] Ethan Park: We have automatic prefix/KV cache in the serving runtime which helps with repeated contexts. For RAG specifically, you manage the retrieval layer but we expose hooks for caching and reuse of KV entries. For heavy RAG usage we often recommend Dedicated or Private to reduce cross-tenant variability.
[10:10] Rajiv Menon: On rollout strategy — if we want to do canary tests and automatic fallbacks to smaller models during congestion, do you support that?
[10:18] Maya Chen: Yes, the Console supports rollouts and routing policies: canary percentage, A/B, and fallback policies to compatible model variants. Those policies can be applied per-route.
[10:35] Kim Alvarez: How do auth and API keys integrate with our tenant model? We need per-customer keys and ability to revoke.
[10:44] Ethan Park: You can create per-tenant API keys and map them to orgs. Keys can be rotated/revoked in the Console or via API. Audit logs show which key made requests.
[11:05] Lara Boyd: Any gotchas for proxying websockets or SSE for streaming behind corporate gateways?
[11:12] Ethan Park: SSEs generally work but require long-lived connections; some corporate proxies will time out idle connections. We recommend keepalive pings or using a relay in the VPC. For WebSocket-based streaming we can also suggest upgrade patterns.
[11:45] Rajiv Menon: For a pilot, what would you recommend as a minimal scope? Hosted quickstart for eval, then Dedicated pilot if we like perf?
[11:55] Maya Chen: Exactly. Start with hosted to move fast, do a benchmark week where we run your QPS/prompt set, then evaluate Dedicated if you need predictability or Private for strict compliance. We'll help with the benchmark harness.
[12:10] Kim Alvarez: Can Redwood integrate into our existing observability stack — we'll want traces tied to request IDs and token-level cost tags.
[12:18] Ethan Park: Yes, we support injecting request IDs and you can pass trace headers. Cost metadata is in the logs and we can include token counts per request.
[12:40] Lara Boyd: Licensing and pricing — high level now?
[12:45] Maya Chen: High level: hosted is usage-based (per token/embeddings), Dedicated is reserved capacity with commit tiers, Private is enterprise licensing. I'll send the pricing matrix and sample TCO for a 6-month pilot.
[13:10] Rajiv Menon: Any references or customers in infra / multi-tenant SaaS space?
[13:15] Maya Chen: Yes, we have several — I'll include two references that have similar scale and compliance needs.
[13:30] Kim Alvarez: Ok, let's dig into a few technical details — Ethan, can you outline the LangChain example live?
[13:36] Ethan Park: (walkthrough) Typical code:
- install redwood sdk
- from redwood import RedwoodClient
- client = RedwoodClient(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_KEY'))
- class RedwoodLLM(LLM): def _call(self, prompt): return client.generate(prompt, model='redwood-rl-small', stream=True)
You'll then hook the streaming callback into LangChain callbacks.
[14:20] Rajiv Menon: For throughput tests, what harness do you recommend?
[14:25] Ethan Park: We usually provide a small Python harness that runs concurrent requests with your prompt templates, measures p50/p95/p99 latency and token usage. We'll run it from your network and from our hosted env to understand network variance.
[15:00] Lara Boyd: About model variants and quantization — can we bring our tuned quantized models to Redwood?
[15:08] Ethan Park: For Private deployments you can bring models; Dedicated supports custom model variants subject to compatibility. For Hosted we onboard curated models; custom models typically go on Dedicated/Private. We also support different quantization profiles; Runtime auto-selects kernels for performance.
[15:35] Kim Alvarez: Are there SDK rate-limit backoff/retry helpers built-in?
[15:40] Ethan Park: Yes, SDK includes exponential backoff and retry strategies and convenience wrappers for idempotency.
[16:00] Rajiv Menon: Anything about tokenization differences across models? Will our token accounting change when switching models?
[16:08] Maya Chen: Tokenization can vary; we expose token counts per-request so you can correlate. Optimize gives guidance on model choice vs cost.
[16:30] Lara Boyd: Let's capture concrete next steps.
[16:35] Maya Chen: We'll send pricing, SOC2, and the LangChain/LlamaIndex sample repo. Ethan will own the benchmark setup. Polaris to share prompt set, desired QPS, and any compliance constraints.
[17:00] Rajiv Menon: Agreed. Also we'd like a small POC — 2 week hosted pilot with limited dataset and mobility to Dedicated if results look good.
[17:07] Maya Chen: Sounds good. We'll draft a pilot plan.

[30:00] (brief technical detour where Ethan and Rajiv discussed kernel selection and batch sizes; some crosstalk, audio briefly overlapped)
[33:12] Ethan Park: Note about KV cache — if you have repeated context across users, KV caching can reduce cost significantly. We can tune TTLs.
[35:50] Kim Alvarez: On logs — we need a per-tenant log stream; will you create separate log streams per org in the hosted offering?
[35:58] Ethan Park: Yes, logs can be scoped per-org and pushed to separate sinks or tags. For strict isolation we recommend Dedicated/Private.
[38:10] Lara Boyd: Any SLA for latency or availability?
[38:16] Maya Chen: Hosted has a baseline SLA; Dedicated/Private offers stronger SLAs and support tiers. We'll include specifics in the follow-up.
[40:00] Rajiv Menon: For the benchmark, can you measure 99th percentile for short prompts and cost per 1k tokens?
[40:08] Ethan Park: Yes — we'll include p50/p95/p99 and cost per 1k tokens in the benchmark report.
[42:30] Kim Alvarez: One last question: we use a shared model store and want to instrument token-level attribution to customers for chargeback. Is that possible?
[42:40] Ethan Park: Yes, per-api-key accounting and token attribution is supported; logs include customer context fields for chargeback.
[43:00] Lara Boyd: Great. Any blockers?
[43:04] Maya Chen: No blockers; small actions. We'll share the docs and schedule the deep dive.
[43:20] Rajiv Menon: Thanks all.
[43:25] Maya Chen: Thanks, we'll follow up today with the materials and set a time for the benchmark kickoff.
[45:20] (meeting ends)

Recap / Next steps in call:
- Redwood to send: pricing matrix, SOC2 + security whitepaper, LangChain & LlamaIndex sample repo, benchmark harness.
- Ethan to run a benchmark week with Polaris prompt set (Polaris to supply prompts and QPS targets).
- Polaris to evaluate hosted pilot, then decide on Dedicated/Private path depending on perf/compliance.
